s.g: A critical or explanatory commentary or analysis.
A comment added to a text.
The process of writing such comment or commentary.
Not exhibiting any symptoms of disease, as for example in a case which is subclinical (“without signs detectable by physical examination or laboratory test”).
Any set of machine-readable parallel bars or concentric circles, varying in width, spacing, or height, encoding information according to a symbology.
A sheltered place where bees, usually honey bees (genus Apis), live.
Any place full of activity, or in which people are very busy.
A women's hairstyle, popular in the 1960s, in which long hair is styled into a hive-shaped form on top of the head and usually held in place with lacquer.
The part of the Earth and its atmosphere capable of supporting life.
A person who uses diet and exercise to build an aesthetically muscular physique, in order to compete in bodybuilding.
(botany) A person engaged in botany, the scientific study of plants.
(uncountable) The state of being calm; tranquillity; silence.
(historical) A medieval kingdom and former county in the Iberian Peninsula; the nucleus of modern Spain.
An early human or closely related species, popularly held to reside in caves.
Divided into a grid of squares of alternating colours or shades, or into light and dark patches.
The stems and leaves of the coriander plant, Coriandrum sativum, used as a seasoning and garnish in cooking.
Of a man, having had the foreskin of the penis excised.
The study of good citizenship and proper membership in a community.

A type of small, sweet-tasting orange, the result of a hybrid cross between the willowleaf variety of mandarin orange (Citrus × aurantium f. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (Citrus sinensis). Scientific name: Citrus × clementina.
A buffer in memory where the user can store data temporarily while transferring it from one place within an application to another or between applications.
A specialist in a given field whose opinion is highly valued, especially in one of the fine arts or in matters of taste.
An assembly or meeting.
The act of calling or assembling by summons.
(ecclesiastical) An assembly of the clergy, by their representatives, to consult on ecclesiastical affairs.
(medicine, botany) A sacklike cavity, a tube open at one end only.
A circular area at the end of a dead end street to allow cars to turn around, designed so children can play on the street, with little or no through-traffic.
Meriting condemnation, censure or blame, especially as something wrong, harmful or injurious; blameworthy, guilty.
(idiomatic, by extension) A prelude or introduction to an activity or thing.
A girl; a maiden (without sexual experience).
The state of being dazed
The act of divining; a foreseeing or foretelling of future events.
Initialism of Democratic People's Republic of Korea, official name of North Korea: a country in East Asia.
A state of being drunk.
(intransitive) To leave the country in which one lives, especially one's native country, in order to reside elsewhere.
A stable suspension of small droplets of one liquid in another with which it is immiscible.

A river in the Middle East, 2780 kilometers in length, flowing southwest from Turkey, then southeast, and uniting with the Tigris before entering the Persian Gulf. It forms the Western edge of classical Mesopotamia.
The ritual act of driving out evil spirits from persons, places or things that are possessed by them.
Made known by fables or reputation; legendary, famed.
To form into a whole by uniting its parts; to construct; to build.
The state of being a father (biological father, stepfather, adoptive father, foster father; sometimes the biological father specifically).
Of, pertaining to, or near the femur or thigh.

(historical) A mercenary soldier; a freebooter; specifically, a mercenary who travelled illegally in an organized group from the United States to a country in Central America or the Spanish West Indies in the mid-19th century seeking economic and political benefits through armed force.
(originally, and, mainly, US politics, intransitive, transitive) To use obstructionist tactics in a legislative body.
(transitive) To make final or firm; to finish or complete.
A thin fabric with a loose, open weave.
A similar bleached cotton fabric used as a surgical dressing.
A demon said to feed on corpses.
A graverobber.
The seating area at a stadium or arena; the bleachers.
A sensory perception of something that does not exist, often arising from disorder of the nervous system, as in delirium tremens.
The act of hallucinating; a wandering of the mind; an error, mistake or blunder.

A sign used in the written Arabic language representing a glottal stop. Hamza may appear as a stand-alone letter (ء (ʔ)) or most commonly diacritically over or under other letters, e.g. أ (ʔ) (over an alif [ا]), إ (ʔ) (under an alif), ؤ (ʔ) (over a wāw [و]) or ئ (ʔ) (over a dotless yāʾ [ى]). The exact seat of hamza is governed by an orthographic rule – the "seat of hamza rule".
(physics, chemistry) Lacking an affinity for water; unable to absorb or to be wetted by water.
Anything which flows in or into.
An independent, telephonic communication system, set up around and throughout a building, complex, or residence, typically for access control.
A general left-wing anthem for solidarity and emancipation of the working class, dating back to the 19th century.
A knight in a medieval romance who wanders in search of adventure and opportunities to prove his chivalry.
An honour whereby one is made into a knight, and whereafter one is entitled to be called Sir.
(figuratively) The one weakness of something or someone that is otherwise invulnerable.
One who uses bodily strength rather than intellect to earn a wage, usually hourly.

Any of various tropical and subtropical evergreen shrubs or trees chiefly of the Rhizophoraceae family that have aerial roots and grow in clumps in brackish intertidal coastal areas; (specifically) any of various trees of the genus Rhizophora, especially the red mangrove (Rhizophora mangle).

A kind of jam made with citrus fruit, distinguished by being made slightly bitter by the addition of the peel and by partial caramelisation during manufacture. Most commonly made with Seville oranges, and usually qualified by the name of the fruit when made with other types of fruit.

(grammar) A word, phrase, or clause that limits or qualifies the sense of another word or phrase. (It may be any of the following: an adjective phrase, an adverb phrase, a prepositional phrase, a noun phrase, or a subordinate clause.)
The Hawaiian goose, Branta sandvicensis, which was designated the state bird of Hawaii in 1957.
To arbitrarily limit or reduce the capability of.

A type of lever used to propel a boat, having a flat blade at one end and a handle at the other, and pivoted in a rowlock atop the gunwale, whereby a rower seated in the boat and pulling the handle can pass the blade through the water by repeated strokes against the water's resistance, thus moving the boat.
Of, pertaining to, or situated in, the occident, or west; western.
A drug, hormone or other substance derived from or related to opium.
A bird of prey of genus Pandion that feeds on fish and has white underparts and long, narrow wings each ending in four finger-like extensions.
(chiefly, Ireland, humorous, informal) Human skin, especially when bare; also, a person's hair.
The skin of an animal with the hair or wool on; either a raw or undressed hide, or a skin preserved with the hair or wool on it (sometimes worn as a garment with minimal modification).
Chiefly followed by at: to (continuously) throw (missiles) at.
To remove the skin from (an animal); to skin.
Of a number of small objects (such as raindrops), or the sun's rays: to beat down or fall on (someone or something) in a shower.
To bombard (someone or something) with missiles.
